text:
Rae: Quick PSA after nightmare on my last trip 10: luggage tips thread. Lost bag at CDG, opened a claim. Sharing what actually helped with the airline and the lessons learned so you don't go through the same.

Tom: Oh no. Major ouch. What helped most?

Rae: Two things: 1) file a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) at the airline desk before leaving the airport, get the reference number on paper/photo. 2) take pics of contents & luggage itself before checking in. Airline asked for photos when I escalated.

Sonia: Also essential: keep meds/one outfit/charger in carry-on. Learned that the hard way. :sob:

claims-bot: quick checklist: PIR at airport -> keep reference (e.g., ABCD1234) -> upload photos of bag and contents -> keep receipts for expensive items -> follow up with claim email within 7 days.

Ben: I carry a small printed inventory in a ziploc inside the suitcase. Cheap stuff but surprisingly useful when they ask "what was inside?" Also note serial numbers for electronics.

Aria: Bonus: put a luggage tag with a secondary contact (local phone + email) and a Tile/Apple AirTag in an internal pocket. If security asks about tracking devices in checked bags, some airlines ask you to declare them; YMMV.

Rae: Timeline I followed: PIR at desk -> they gave a ref -> airline texted a link to upload photos -> they sent an interim message claiming they'd search 48-72h -> after 5 days, bag delivered to hotel with minor scuffs. If they don't find it, open formal claim and keep receipts.

Tom: Any templates for the claim email?

Rae: I used something short: ```
Subject: Lost baggage claim - PIR <REF>
Hi <airline team>,
My bag (brand/color) was lost on flight <XX123> on <date>. PIR ref: <REF>. Photos and itemized list attached. Please advise next steps and compensation process.
Thanks,
<Name>
```

Sonia: If they offer a daily allowance for essentials, use a credit card that covers travel delays/lost baggage for faster reimbursement. Check card T&C first.

Ben: Pro tip: when you check the PIR, write down the agent name and counter number. When I had to argue, having the person who processed it made follow-ups easier.

Aria: Also, if you're traveling for an offsite and have company kit in the checked bag, mark that in claim and notify ops/support early. They can sometimes ship a spare laptop or badge.

Rae: TL;DR: file PIR at airport, photos + inventory, keep essentials on you, use tracker, and keep receipts. Poll: react with :white_check_mark: if you have a tracker in your luggage, :x: if you don't, or reply "never checked" if you always carry everything on.
